006fed1f  b8 d8 5a 83 00   mov     eax, 0x835ad8  ; Primary MsgAction (type 10010) dispatcher. Jump action 0x89 at 0x700352..0x7003DE requires the packet entity id at +0x04 to resolve to a role. For a non-local role it resets a 0x11C command block, writes command type 0x14 + (packet byte +0x24 != 0), widens packet uint16 coordinates at +0x08/+0x0A into command target dwords +0x208/+0x20C, then invokes the role command-state apply callback. The local-role echo branch instead updates the local hero coordinate gate from the same +0x08/+0x0A pair. Verified audio path: action type 0x7C resolves the sound path via GameDataSetQuery()->vtable[+0x30] using packet sound id at +0x08, then calls _DXPlaySound@24 with default parameters (x=0, y=0, range=0, loop=0, volume=100).

DISPATCH KEY: first switch on word [packet+0x14] (0x6FED46). Early-handled keys: 0x4A (0x6FEE14 OVERWRITES packet+4 with local hero id +0xCC, then joins common path), 0x5E, 0x65, 0x68, >0x6A etc.

COMMON ENTITY GATE (CORRECTED 2026-09-28): 0x6FF15D..0x6FF18A calls
EntityRef_ResolveByIdOrLocalHero(&g_objPlayerSet, &ref, packet+4, includeLocalHero=1).
  resolved   -> 0x6FF231 main switch (rung branches below)
  unresolved -> only 0x4F/0x51/0x63/0x82/0x89 continue (0x6FF1B0: send MsgAction 0x66 with packet+4);
                every other key incl. 0x4B/0x4C/0x4D/0x4E/0x61 exits at 0x700974 WITHOUT advancing.
So echoed entity id at +4 IS observed on rungs 0x4B..0x4E/0x61: must be local hero id (or an id in g_objPlayerSet). 0x4A is immune (overwritten at 0x6FEE14).

TIMESTAMP (+0x10) read only at 0x6FEF51, 0x6FF05F, 0x6FF952, 0x700373, 0x7006E7; never on ladder.

LADDER (main switch 0x6FF262.. sub 0x4A/dec): inbound 0x4A -> 0x6FF44A sends 0x4B; 0x4B -> 0x6FF3CD sends 0x4C then posts main msg 0x401; 0x4C -> 0x6FF365 sends 0x4D; 0x4D -> 0x6FF2FA sends 0x4E; 0x4E -> 0x6FF283 sends 0x61. Each rung builds CMsgAction__Create(heroId=CHero+0xCC,0,0,0,next) - no other packet field or state read.

006fed4c  0f 8f 23 02 00 00 jg      0x6fef75  ; CMsgAction__Process dispatch head. The action id is the u16 at packet+0x14. Dispatch is NOT one switch: it is a hand-written mix of direct compares, cascaded "sub reg, imm / jz" chains (the compiler idiom for sparse switches, which HLIL folds so the individual ids do not appear in the decompilation), and a jump-table switch at 0x70011D covering 0x80..0x9F. Reading the ids off HLIL alone will miss most of them - 108, for one, is dispatched by the cascade at 0x6FFC48 (0x6FFC27 cmp 0x6F, then sub 0x64 / sub 3 / sub 5), which no HLIL case label shows.

DO NOT treat any list of ids extracted from this function as complete unless it was built from the disassembly with the cascades accumulated and the 0x80..0x9F table expanded.

What IS established here, for 408 (0x198): the constant 0x198 does not appear ANYWHERE in this function's disassembly - not as a compare, not as a cascade total, not in the jump-table range. The client therefore has no inbound handler for action 408, and there is nothing a server could send under that id that this client would act on. Dropping an inbound 408 is complete and correct behaviour, not an unimplemented one.

The client SENDS 408 itself from seven known sites. CORRECTION: an earlier version of this comment called them all equipment work and named the action accordingly - that was wrong. The sites are the four MsgTick apply branches (0x6EB099 subtype 17, 0x6EB2ED unequip, 0x6EB51D equip, 0x6EB6F5 subtype 18), both equipment-set switch paths in sub_6DAEB9 (right after MsgTick subtype 0x2C / 0x2D), and CMsgMapInfo1110__Process at 0x732D38, which sends it after applying a new map - not equipment at all. What the seven share is that each has just finished refreshing hero-visible state; several of them post 0x445/0x446 immediately before. Every site builds it as CMsgAction__BuildType10010(message, 0x198, 0), so it carries no fields.
